en.title: Alternating Diagonal Traversal of a Matrix
en.description:
Starting from the top-left corner, traverse the diagonals in increasing order of the row-plus-column index sum. Even index sums go from bottom-left to top-right, and odd index sums go from top-right to bottom-left. Output the traversal sequence. The order in the original site's 3×3 example is wrong, so this site corrects it according to the standard alternating rule.

The input format, examples, and test data were compiled and written by CSWork.
en.input: This site's input scale: R C (1..100), followed by R lines of C integers each (−10⁹..10⁹).
en.output: Output the answer as described; separate multiple results with spaces in order, and output an empty line for an empty array.
en.explanation: Example 1: the diagonals output [1], [2,4], [7,5,3], [6,8], [9] in order, and concatenating them gives the result.
hints: Enumerate the index sum d and determine the valid range of row indices on that diagonal. For even d, go through the row indices in reverse; for odd d, in forward order.
